sourceFindings.finding: Messages has no send/search/conversation handlers; those controls are disabled. MAP discovery and reserved tables do not implement messaging.
No concrete IDeviceTransport implementation was found. Existing connections are separate components, not a unified engine.
RequestDialAsync selects the first connected trusted iPhone rather than an explicit user-selected target. Fix before exposing multi-device command workflows.
Architecture/threat documents include future objectives: Generic Host/MVVM/SwiftData, durable commands, key rotation and other controls cannot be assumed shipped.
Raw exception.Message reaches some debug/UI paths. Redaction/canary review is required; this is a potential exposure path, not a demonstrated private-data leak.
Frozen security policy checkboxes and initially disabled eligibility-gated buttons are not automatically placeholders. Distinguish those from the unwired messaging UI.
No NotImplementedException or TODO marker was found by the scoped production-source search. That does not prove feature completeness; absent handlers/providers are stronger evidence.

schemaCaveat: Based on scoped executable SQL/source searches, not a promise that migration/test references do not exist. Do not drop tables or infer corresponding features from their existence.
physicalConnectionGates: Owner reports phone disconnected; no phone probe or authorization change was performed for this assessment.
Owner chose Windows sideloading. The staged Sideloadly installer reports Authenticode NotSigned and has not been executed; execution/dependency review remains explicit.
The companion IPA is unsigned and contains no provisioning profile; signing/install/launch remain unverified.
Owner must handle Apple account authentication, developer trust/Developer Mode and phone permissions. No credentials in chat, logs, source or public CI.
The old Windows MSIX predates later features; package identity and direct-launch protected data stores differ, without automatic trust migration.
Persistent Windows phone-transport registration and audible receiver testing are separate pending approvals, not implied by choosing iOS sideloading.
firstConnectionAcceptance: Owner-selected signing route installs and launches the current companion without bypassing security.
Both devices review a fresh QR offer and explicitly confirm matching six words.
Windows shows an authenticated current session, not merely USB/Bluetooth presence.
One reviewed health snapshot receives a correlated acceptance receipt in that session.
A disconnect/reconnect authenticates again; a revoked peer cannot reconnect.
Only then verify permitted Contacts and a small selected photo on the physical phone.
implementationChangesDuringAssessment: None to production code, permissions, entitlements or database schema. This report is an assessment artifact, not a new runtime capability.
